items.title: Cause and Result Close the Existing-Things Framework Entirely

items.zh: 何等名為因相有法？當知此因略有五種。一、可愛因，二、不可愛因，三、長養因，四、流轉因，五、還滅因。可愛因者，謂善有漏法。不可愛因者，謂不善法。
items.en: What is called a thing existing by the mark of a cause? Know that, briefly, this cause has five kinds: first, the cause of what is desirable; second, the cause of what is undesirable; third, the cause of nurturing growth; fourth, the cause of continued flow; and fifth, the cause of reversal and cessation. The cause of what is desirable: wholesome but still-defiled phenomena. The cause of what is undesirable: unwholesome phenomena.

items.zh: 長養因者，謂前前所生善、不善、無記法，修習、善修習、多修習故，能令後後所生善、不善、無記法展轉增勝，名長養因。流轉因者，謂由此種子，由此薰習，由此助伴，彼法流轉，此於彼法，名流轉因。
items.en: The cause of nurturing growth: wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral action already produced, which, through practice, skilful practice, and repeated practice, causes wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral action produced afterwards to grow progressively stronger — this is called the cause of nurturing growth. The cause of continued flow: through this seed, through this habituation, through these accompanying conditions, that phenomenon continues to flow onward. In relation to that phenomenon, this is called the cause of continued flow.

items.zh: 還滅因者，謂諸行還滅、雜染還滅，所有一切能寂靜道、能般涅槃、能趣菩提，及彼資糧，并其方便，能生能辦，名還滅因。如是總名因相有法。
items.en: The cause of reversal and cessation: whatever pacifies conditioned formations, reverses defilement, and — including the path itself, the requisites for it, and the skilful means leading to it — is capable of bringing about nirvāṇa, of leading towards awakening, and of actually producing and accomplishing this: this is called the cause of reversal and cessation. All of this together is called existence by the mark of a cause.

items.zh: 若廣分別，如思因果中應知其相。
何等名為果相有法？謂從彼五因，若生、若得、若成、若辦、若轉，當知是名果相有法。
items.en: What is called a thing existing by the mark of a result? Whatever arises, is attained, is accomplished, is brought about, or is transformed, in dependence on those five causes — know that this is called existence by the mark of a result.

items.title: Non-Existing Things: Five Ways Something Genuinely Has No Real Mark

items.zh: 何等名為所觀無法？當知此相亦有五種。一、未生無，二、已滅無，三、互相無，四、勝義無，五、畢竟無。未生無者，謂未來諸行。已滅無者，謂過去諸行。
items.en: What is called a non-existing thing under examination? Know that this mark, too, has five kinds: first, not-yet-arisen non-existence; second, already-ceased non-existence; third, mutual non-existence; fourth, ultimate non-existence; and fifth, absolute non-existence. Not-yet-arisen non-existence: future conditioned things. Already-ceased non-existence: past conditioned things.

items.zh: 互相無者，謂諸餘法，由所餘相若遠離性、若非有性；或所餘法，與諸餘法不和合性。勝義無者，謂由世俗言說自性，假設言論所安立性。
items.en: Mutual non-existence: among various things, one thing's mark being either entirely absent from another, or of an altogether different nature from it; or one thing standing in a relation of simple incompatibility with another. Ultimate non-existence: the nature set up by provisional expression, on the basis of the self-nature of conventional speech.

items.zh: 畢竟無者，謂石女兒等，畢竟無類。
items.en: Absolute non-existence: as with "the child of a barren woman" — something belonging to a category that could never exist in the first place.

items.title: Reflecting on What Is Cognized Concludes: The Same Ground, Seen Through Being and Non-Being

items.zh: 復有五種有性、五種無性。何等名為五種有性？一、圓成實相有性，二、依他起相有性，三、遍計所執相有性，四、差別相有性，五、不可說相有性。此中，初是勝義相。第二是緣生相相。第三是假施設相。第四是不二相。生相、老相、住相、無常相、苦相、空相、無我相、事相、所識相、所取相、淨妙等相、饒益等相、言說相相、邪行等相相。如是等相，應知名差別相。第五由四種不可說故，名不可說相。
items.en: There are, further, five kinds of having a nature and five kinds of lacking a nature. What are the five kinds of having a nature? First, the nature of the perfectly real mark; second, the nature of the dependent mark; third, the nature of the imagined mark; fourth, the nature of the differentiated mark; and fifth, the nature of the inexpressible mark. Of these, the first is the mark of ultimate meaning. The second is the mark of dependently-arisen appearance. The third is the mark of merely provisional designation. The fourth is the mark of non-duality [with the aggregates]. The fifth is called inexpressible for four reasons.

items.zh: 一、無故不可說。謂補特伽羅於彼諸蘊，不可宣說若異不異。二、甚深故不可說。謂離言法性不可思議，如來法身不可思議。諸佛境界，如來滅後若有若無等，不可宣說。三、能引無義故不可說。謂若諸法，非能引發法義梵行，諸佛世尊雖證不說。四、法相法爾之所安立故不可說。所謂真如於諸行等，不可宣說異不異性。
items.en: First, inexpressible because it does not exist [as with the person, which cannot be declared either different or not different from the aggregates]. Second, inexpressible because it is too profound — the nature beyond words is inconceivable, the Tathāgata's own body of truth is inconceivable. Third, inexpressible because expressing it would serve no genuine purpose. Fourth, inexpressible because this is simply how the nature of things is: suchness cannot be declared either the same as, or different from, conditioned phenomena.

items.zh: 何等名為五種無性？一、勝義相無性，二、自依相無性，三、畢竟自相無性，四、無差別相無性，五、可說相無性。
items.en: What are the five kinds of lacking a nature? First, the ultimate mark's absence of [a self or phenomena's] nature; second, absence of a self-dependent nature; third, absolute absence of the imagined nature's own mark; fourth, absence of a real nature in any differentiated mark; and fifth, absence of any genuinely expressible mark.

items.title: Reflecting on the Teachings Opens: Sutra and Verse, and No-Self's Opening Line

items.zh: 云何思擇諸法？此復二種應知。一、思擇素呾纜義，二、思擇伽他義。思擇素呾纜義，如攝事分及菩薩藏教授中當廣說。
items.en: What is reflecting on the teachings? Know that this again has two kinds: first, reflecting on the meaning of sutras; and second, reflecting on the meaning of verses. Reflecting on the meaning of sutras will be broadly explained in the Compendium of Topics and in the bodhisattva canon's own instruction.

items.zh: 思擇伽他義，復有三種。一者、建立勝義伽他，二者、建立意趣義伽他，三者、建立體義伽他。
items.en: Reflecting on the meaning of verses again has three kinds: first, establishing the ultimate-meaning verses; second, establishing the verses on essential intent; and third, establishing the verses on the essential body of the teaching.

items.zh: 建立勝義伽他者，如經言：都無有宰主及作者、受者；諸法亦無用，而用轉非無。
items.en: Establishing the ultimate-meaning verses: as the scripture says — there is no sovereign master, no doer and no experiencer; the constituents of a person have no such function of their own, yet the very functioning that occurs is not simply nothing.

items.title: No-Self, Verses 2–9: No Ruler Anywhere, No Function Standing on Its Own

items.zh: 唯十二有支、蘊、處、界、流轉。審思此一切，眾生不可得。於內及於外，是一切皆空。其能修空者，亦常無所有。我我定非有；由顛倒妄計。有情、我皆無；唯有因法有。
items.en: There are only the twelve links of dependent origination, flowing on as aggregates, sense-fields, and elements; examine all of this carefully, and no sentient being is to be found. Within and without, all of it is empty; even one who cultivates this very emptiness is, in the end, nowhere to be found. The self [of the noble] and the self [of ordinary beings] definitely do not exist — they are posited only through inverted, false conception; no being and no self exist at all — there exists only what arises through causes.

items.zh: 諸行皆剎那，住尚無，況用。即說彼生起，為用，為作者。眼不能見色，耳不能聞聲，鼻不能嗅香，舌不能甞味，身不能覺觸，意不能知法。於此，亦無能任持驅役者。法不能生他，亦不能自生。眾緣有，故生，非故，新新有。法不能滅他，亦不能自滅。眾緣有，故生，生已，自然滅。
items.en: All conditioned things are momentary — they do not even abide, let alone truly function; what is called their arising is merely spoken of as function, as an agent. The eye cannot itself see form; the ear cannot itself hear sound; the nose cannot itself smell fragrance; the tongue cannot itself taste flavour; the body cannot itself feel contact; the mind cannot itself know a mental object — and within all this there is no controller, no one directing or driving it. No phenomenon can produce another, nor can it produce itself; because the many conditions are present, it arises — not as something old continuing, but ever newly, freshly present. No phenomenon can extinguish another, nor can it extinguish itself; because the many conditions were present, it arose, and having arisen, it naturally ceases.

blocks.text: Today completes the sorting of what exists and what does not, and turns to the third aspect: reflecting on the teachings. The treatise presents a set of forty-four "verses of ultimate meaning" on non-self, among the most important passages in the treatise. Ru-Yi translates the verses; the prose commentary on them, from Day 129, is largely untranslated, and the commentary will summarise it.

The last two kinds of existence: as **cause** (desirable, undesirable, nurturing, continuing, reversing) and as **result**. Venerable Miào Jìng: what makes a cause desirable or undesirable is the motive: "the outward action may please people, but if the motive is bad, that is an undesirable cause." The cause of "continued flow" works, the *Pīxún jì* explains, through seeds, karma, and ignorance; the cause of "reversal" is the path.

Things may not exist in five ways: not yet arisen (Master Cháng Bǎi: "yourself ten years from now"); already ceased; mutually absent (Venerable Miào Jìng: "an ox has no horse-nature, and a horse no ox-nature"), including incompatibility, as when right mindfulness arises and the bad thought is gone; ultimately non-existent; and absolutely non-existent, like "a barren woman's child".

subs.head: The same ground, seen through being and non-being

blocks.text: Five kinds of being and five of non-being are then mapped onto the three natures. Master Cháng Bǎi on the imagined nature: what is imagined lacks substance, "but the clinging itself exists"; the clinging mind and its image are dependent. Venerable Miào Jìng on "other-emptiness": the ultimate itself exists, but lacks self and proliferation. And on suchness: "you cannot leave conditioned phenomena and speak of a separate unborn, unceasing suchness."

Reflection on the scriptures covers sūtra and verse. Sūtra reflection is deferred to the *Compendium of Topics* (fascicles 85–100). Verses are of three kinds: of ultimate meaning, of intent, and of essential body (Venerable Miào Jìng: the last tell you the practices).

The verses of ultimate meaning begin: "There is no ruler, no agent, no experiencer; dharmas have no function, yet functioning is not absent." There are "only the twelve links, flowing as aggregates, sense-fields, and elements". Venerable Miào Jìng: the twelve links are the vertical account, the aggregates the horizontal; "the ignorance link isn't just ignorance alone; within it are the five aggregates."

"Not old continuing, but ever new": nothing lasts a moment. "No phenomenon can extinguish another; having arisen, it ceases of itself." Venerable Miào Jìng: arising needs conditions; ceasing does not. This is the momentariness of Day 18 stated in verse.

quiz.q: The desirable cause is wholesome action; the undesirable, unwholesome. Where does Venerable Miào Jìng locate the deciding factor?
options: the motive — an action may look pleasing, but if the motive is bad, it's an undesirable cause
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The outward action may please people, but if the motive is bad, that is an undesirable cause." Master Cháng Bǎi: the desirable cause is contaminated good such as the five precepts and ten good deeds.

quiz.q: The cause of continued flow works "through seed, habituation, and accompanying conditions." How does the Pixunji explain them?
options: seeds of dharmas bound to the three realms; habituation is pure and impure karma; accompaniment is ignorance, craving, grasping — the origin truth as the cause of flow
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "The seeds are those of dharmas bound to the three realms; habituation is pure and impure karma; the accompaniments are ignorance, craving, and grasping. This presents the origin truth as the cause of flow."

quiz.q: For mutual non-existence by "entire absence," what example does Venerable Miào Jìng himself give?
options: an ox lacks the nature of a horse and a horse that of an ox — each lacks the other
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "An ox has no horse-nature, and a horse no ox-nature — each lacks the other: mutual non-existence." The *Pixunji* he then reads uses resistant form and space instead.

quiz.q: Absolute non-existence is "a barren woman's child." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: a woman who cannot bear children claiming a son — no such thing; hence absolute non-existence
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "A woman who doesn't bear children saying she has a son — how could that be? So this is called absolute non-existence." A merely absent tree is not the same category.

quiz.q: The imagined nature lacks both substance and mark — why is it still among the five "having a nature," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: what is imagined lacks substance, but the act of clinging remains — the clinging mind and the image it holds still exist
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though what is imagined lacks substance and mark, the clinging itself exists — the clinging mind and the clung-to image are still there. Venerable Miào Jìng: without clinging there would be no ordinary beings.

quiz.q: The note speaks of "two sets of verses." How many kinds does the treatise list, and what is the theme of the ultimate-meaning verses?
options: three (ultimate, intent, essential body); the ultimate verses teach the emptiness of self — neither identical with nor apart from the aggregates is there a permanent controlling self
quiz.why: The treatise lists three kinds. Master Cháng Bǎi: the contemplation of selflessness shows that neither identical with nor apart from the aggregates is there the permanent, unchanging, controlling self ordinary beings imagine.

quiz.q: "Only the twelve links, flowing as aggregates, sense-fields, and elements." How does Venerable Miào Jìng relate the two?
options: the twelve links are the vertical account, aggregates and the rest the horizontal — even the ignorance link contains aggregates, fields, and elements
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The ignorance link isn't just ignorance alone; within it are the five aggregates, twelve fields, and eighteen elements." The links are vertical, the aggregates horizontal.
